html:
Dian Fossey was an American zoologist who studied the mountain gorillas of the Virunga volcanoes in Rwanda from 1967 until she was murdered at her camp in 1985.

Encouraged by Louis Leakey, she founded the Karisoke research centre and lived among gorilla groups for years, showing they were gentle and social animals. She fought poachers fiercely, and her killing has never been solved. Her book Gorillas in the Mist was made into a film in 1988.

The gorillas she studied survived, and their number has since risen. Paid visits to see them in Volcanoes National Park became a major source of income for Rwanda, tied to the post-war image of Kigali as a safe place to visit.
sum: Dian Fossey was an American zoologist who studied the mountain gorillas of the Virunga volcanoes in Rwanda from 1967 until she was murdered at her camp in 1985.
